title: PSC system reference: controlled-substance agreement signature on Prescriptions & Renewals
content:
**Subject.** For a controlled prescription of the Prescriptions & Renewals line — a Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription or a Schedule II Controlled Prescription — the patient may sign a new controlled-substance agreement. When the patient signs a new controlled-substance agreement for a controlled prescription, the agreement sets the agreed fill interval, which is recorded on the prescription as its per-fill days' supply on the day the patient signs. Signing the agreement is the patient's own act, and the patient accepts the agreed fill interval by signing.

**Business effect of one signature.** The prescription record shows that day as the date the patient signed the controlled-substance agreement, and its per-fill days' supply becomes the agreed fill interval. Nothing else on the prescription changes.

### Situation of use and capability

The tool records, on one controlled prescription of the patient, that the patient signed a new controlled-substance agreement today, and sets that prescription's per-fill days' supply to the value given.

### How it is invoked

The tool is `sign_controlled_agreement_46ef2e3a`. It is the patient's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves (the patient) runs it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `prescription_id` | reference number of the controlled prescription the agreement covers, as shown by the prescription lookup for this patient | identifier |
| `days_supply` | days' supply each fill of the prescription dispenses under the signed agreement | whole number of days written as an integer greater than 0, no decimals and no unit text |

The tool has no enumerated parameters.

### Return

On success the receipt is a dictionary: `prescription_id`, `controlled_agreement_signed_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `days_supply` (integer days per fill now recorded) and `status`, which reads "signed" when the signature is recorded. Afterwards the prescription lookup shows today's date as the agreement signature date and the new per-fill days' supply. No other return or error is defined for the tool.

### Questions on the contract

*Does the signature change the fills the prescription still authorizes or its expiration date?* No; only the agreement signature date and the per-fill days' supply change.

*Who runs the tool?* The patient, after the agent has unlocked it and handed it over.
